name: Qalandar Bakhsh Jurat
bio: Jurat of Delhi is described in the book as celebrated for his skill in music, astronomy and poetry; he became blind while still young and was pensioned by Nawab Muhabbat Khan and afterwards by Suleiman Shikoh. He is the author of an enormous volume of ghazals and love-poems in the modern taste, and also wrote satires on the rain, the cold, smallpox and the like.

The one piece given here is drawn from Hindustani Lyrics (London: The Sufi Publishing Society, 1919), in the English verse of Inayat Khan and Jessie Duncan Westbrook. It is a free rendering, not a literal translation, and the original Urdu poem is untitled; it is named here by its first line.

poems.title: How can I win that Hidden One
poems.author: Qalandar Bakhsh Jurat
poems.translator: trans. Inayat Khan and Jessie Duncan Westbrook (1919)
poems.text:
How can I win that Hidden One
    Who sits within the secret place?
For even in my very dreams
    She wears the veil upon her face.

What heart is there in all the world
    Can bear thy cruel tyranny?
Keep then this broken heart of mine
    That thus thou mayst remember me!
